name: The Fair Nut and String
description: The Fair Nut found a string $$$s$$$. The string consists of lowercase Latin letters. The Nut is a curious guy, so he wants to find the number of strictly increasing sequences $$$p_1, p_2, \ldots, p_k$$$, such that: For each $$$i$$$ ($$$1 \leq i \leq k$$$), $$$s_{p_i} =$$$ 'a' . For each $$$i$$$ ($$$1 \leq i \lt k$$$), there is such $$$j$$$ that $$$p_i \lt j \lt p_{i + 1}$$$ and $$$s_j =$$$ 'b' . The Nut is upset because he doesn't know how to find the number. Help him. This number should be calculated modulo $$$10^9 + 7$$$.
input_specification: The first line contains the string $$$s$$$ ($$$1 \leq |s| \leq 10^5$$$) consisting of lowercase Latin letters.
output_specification: In a single line print the answer to the problem — the number of such sequences $$$p_1, p_2, \ldots, p_k$$$ modulo $$$10^9 + 7$$$.
approach_summary: Apply Knapsack and Basic Dynamic Programming paradigm under the Dynamic Programming (DP) framework. Exploit problem invariants to reduce state space and achieve optimal complexity.
